examples.text: "Hier, ich wollte mal fragen: Ist im Dezember wirklich die Wolle alle? Und wird die Seife gestreckt?"
examples.ref: 1935, Josef Altrichter, editor, Unser Kampf: 200 Beispiele aus dem antifaschistischen Kampf in Deutschland, page 82:
examples.english: "Hey, so I wanted to ask: Are we really going to run out of wool in December? And is the soap being stretched?"

examples.text: Immer wieder kam ja halt von meiner Schwester: "Hier, weißt du was, wenn du auch jetzt nach Kenia gehst, ich werde dich nicht weiter unterstützen".
examples.ref: 2024 March 15, 0:50:56 from the start, in Wohin uns die Sehnsucht treibt | SWR Nachtcafé (television production), spoken by Akoth Sewe, via SWR:
examples.english: See, my sister kept telling me: "Listen, you know what, if you're also going to Kenya now, I'm not going to support you any longer."

raw.etymology_text:
From Middle High German hier, from Old High German hier, from Proto-West Germanic *hēr. Cognate with Dutch hier, English here, Swedish här.
The predominant form in Middle High German and throughout modern dialects of High German is hie (and variants) with loss of the final -r. The form hier began to gain ground from the late 16th century (in spite of Luther’s usage), which may point to influence by cognate Middle Low German hīr, hēr (where no r-less form seems to exist; but compare modern Limburgish heej).
